extracted.intended_audience: nonprofit advocates working on child nutrition (school meals, SNAP, WIC, summer meal programs)
extracted.subtask_short: commenting on federal child nutrition rules
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for nonprofit advocates on drafting and submitting effective public comments to federal agencies (especially USDA/FNS) concerning child nutrition programs, including preparatory steps, structure, evidentiary expectations, and procedural tips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read the proposed rule and accompanying preamble
rubrics_metrics.description: Before you write: Read the proposed rule and accompanying preamble.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand the agency's stated rationale, legal basis, and the specific regulatory language being proposed so your comment can engage directly with the agency's reasoning and text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify specific provisions affecting child nutrition programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Before you write: Identify the specific provisions affecting child nutrition programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pinpoint which sections, definitions, or regulatory changes will affect school meals, SNAP, WIC, SFSP, CACFP, etc., so comments can be targeted and concrete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate with state agency contacts and partner organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Before you write: Coordinate with your state agency contacts and partner organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align facts, data, and policy asks across stakeholders to avoid conflicting submissions and to amplify consistent messaging; use state contacts for local participation numbers or implementation insights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider sign-on letters for amplification
rubrics_metrics.description: Before you write: Consider sign-on letters for amplification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use coalition or multi-organization letters to show broad support or opposition; coordinate timing and lead authorship so the sign-on letter is coherent and submitted within the comment period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of organization/individual and connection to child nutrition
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure: Begin by identifying the organization or individual and their connection to child nutrition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State your standing and why your perspective matters (e.g., service provider, state agency partner, researcher, parent) to establish credibility and relevance to the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of position
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure: Provide a clear statement of position (support, oppose, conditional).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make your overall stance explicit early so reviewers know whether subsequent comments recommend adoption, rejection, or modification of the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific section-by-section comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure: Offer specific, section-by-section comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond directly to particular regulatory provisions and cite paragraph or regulatory text so the agency can easily map your input to proposed rule language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include stories from those affected (anonymized if appropriate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure: Include stories from those affected, anonymized when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal narratives illustrate real-world consequences; anonymize identifiable details as needed for privacy and to protect participants, but be specific about impacts and contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide data on program participation, hunger rates, child outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure: Include relevant data such as program participation, hunger rates, and child outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use quantitative evidence to bolster claims; cite state or program-level statistics when possible to show scale and significance of impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer specific suggested changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure: Provide specific suggested changes to the proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft alternative regulatory text or concrete edits so agencies can adopt your recommendations directly; vague objections are less useful than precise language changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusion with a clear ask
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure: End with a conclusion that contains a clear ask.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize the requested outcome (e.g., withdraw provision, adopt alternative language, conduct more analysis) so the agency has an unambiguous record of requested action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite specific USDA FNS instructions, memos, and prior guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: What makes comments effective: Cite specific USDA FNS instructions, memos, and prior guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference existing agency materials to show how a proposal aligns or conflicts with current practice and to demonstrate technical familiarity with implementation details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference relevant statutes and named programs
rubrics_metrics.description: What makes comments effective: Reference the Healthy, Hunger-Free Kids Act and Russell-Ginnis programs (as applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground arguments in statute and established program frameworks to demonstrate legal and policy context; cite program names and statutory provisions that are implicated by the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide state participation data
rubrics_metrics.description: What makes comments effective: Provide state participation data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use state-specific figures to show how proposed changes would affect participation locally and to highlight variation in program implementation across states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite USDA ERS food security data
rubrics_metrics.description: What makes comments effective: Cite USDA's own ERS food security data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use authoritative federal data sources to support claims about food insecurity trends and program impacts rather than relying solely on anecdote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address impacts on specific child populations
rubrics_metrics.description: What makes comments effective: Address impacts on specific child populations (rural, urban, AI/AN, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disaggregate analysis to show differential impacts on subpopulations (e.g., rural schools, American Indian/Alaska Native communities) and explain equity implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with administrative burden on implementers
rubrics_metrics.description: What makes comments effective: Engage with administrative burden on schools, states, and providers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss implementation costs, staff time, and logistical challenges for institutions that operate nutrition programs to highlight feasibility and unintended consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite peer-reviewed research on program effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: What makes comments effective: Cite peer-reviewed research on nutrition program effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support claims with scholarly literature on outcomes (health, educational, economic) to strengthen technical credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference cost-effectiveness analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: What makes comments effective: Reference cost-effectiveness analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide or cite economic analyses that compare benefits and costs of alternatives to bolster arguments about policy trade-offs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address food waste, nutrition standards, and access dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: What makes comments effective: Address food waste, nutrition standards, and access dimensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider operational and quality-related aspects such as how changes affect food waste, adherence to nutrition standards, and children's access to meals.

rubrics_metrics.name: School meal pattern and nutrition standards (sample topic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample topic: School meal pattern and nutrition standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments may focus on proposed changes to meal requirements, nutrient targets, menu planning, and compliance mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community Eligibility Provision thresholds (sample topic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample topic: Community Eligibility Provision thresholds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address how changes to CEP eligibility or thresholds affect school participation, district finances, and student access to free meals.

rubrics_metrics.name: SNAP work requirements and time limits (sample topic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample topic: SNAP work requirements and time limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments may analyze likely effects on household food security, administrative burden, and caseloads when work rules or time limits are proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summer EBT eligibility and amounts (sample topic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample topic: Summer EBT eligibility and benefit amounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss how proposed eligibility criteria and benefit levels would affect summer food access and program reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: WIC food package contents (sample topic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample topic: WIC food package contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate proposed changes to allowable WIC foods for nutrition appropriateness, cultural relevance, supply-chain feasibility, and participant acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: CACFP reimbursement (sample topic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample topic: Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) reimbursement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on reimbursement rates, eligibility, or administrative changes that affect centers, family providers, and meal quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: SFSP site eligibility (sample topic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample topic: Summer Food Service Program (SFSP) site eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address proposed site standards, geographic or demographic criteria, and impacts on summer meal access for children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit comments early in the period
rubrics_metrics.description: Action tip: Submit comments early in the comment period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early submission helps avoid deadlines-related issues and ensures your comment is in the record even if technical problems occur near the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Save your tracking number
rubrics_metrics.description: Action tip: Save your tracking number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep evidence of submission (tracking number or confirmation) to prove participation in the administrative record if needed later for follow-up or litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share with partners to amplify
rubrics_metrics.description: Action tip: Share your comment with partners to amplify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate dissemination so allied organizations can repost, summarize, or submit complementary comments to increase visibility and pressure on the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track agency response in the final rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Action tip: Track the agency's response in the final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review the agency's preamble to see how it addressed public comments and whether the final decision reflects the record; use this tracking to inform next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare for litigation if final rule departs from comment record
rubrics_metrics.description: Action tip: Prepare for litigation if the final rule departs from the comment record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the agency fails to address material issues raised in comments or makes arbitrary departures, plan for potential administrative or judicial review by preserving the record and consulting counsel.
